discovery: Quantum key distribution: physically secured cryptography based on quantum measurement and entanglement

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the disturbance caused by measuring quantum states can guarantee secret key distribution, giving the first cryptographic security that rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. Ekert (1991) independently linked key security to entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities. This opened the way to device-independent security and certified randomness, and it turned the foundations of quantum nonlocality into a working resource. Their ideas started a whole field of experimental physics. QKD has been carried over hundreds of kilometres of fibre, through turbulent free-space links in daylight, and between ground stations and orbiting satellites, including intercontinental satellite links. It is now moving into national and European infrastructure such as EuroQCI. Few conceptual discoveries have done so much to bring quantum mechanics out of the laboratory into real-world technology.
